answers.q1: Yarn 1 (classic), v1.22.22 as pinned by packageManager in package.json. It's a yarn workspaces monorepo, so use yarn rather than npm or pnpm. Install with: yarn install
answers.q2: yarn test:app --watch=false (CI runs `yarn test:app`. Plain `yarn test` is the same vitest command but starts in watch mode.) The full local gate, including typecheck, eslint and prettier, is: yarn test:all
answers.q4: These are the commands CI's lint workflow runs, in this order: yarn test:other && yarn test:code && yarn test:typecheck. They expand to: prettier --list-different on css, scss, json, md, html and yml files, then eslint --max-warnings=0 --ext .js,.ts,.tsx ., then tsc. To auto-fix, run yarn fix.
answers.q5: Lockfiles yarn.lock and dev-docs/yarn.lock are generated. packages/excalidraw/locales/percentages.json is generated by the locales-coverage script. The other locale files under packages/excalidraw/locales are managed through Crowdin (see crowdin.yml), so only en.json should be edited by hand. Vendored or binary assets: packages/excalidraw/fonts/* (font files) and packages/excalidraw/subset/harfbuzz and packages/excalidraw/subset/woff2 (vendored wasm and woff2 code). Build output and dependencies, none of which are committed: node_modules/, build/, dist/, dev-dist, coverage, public/workbox, packages/excalidraw/types.

q1.reason: Yarn classic with `yarn install` matches the accepted answer.

q2.reason: `yarn test:app --watch=false` is accepted, and `yarn test:all` is correctly described as the superset gate.

q3.reason: `yarn vitest run packages/element/tests/bounds.test.ts` matches the accepted command exactly.

q4.reason: It gives the CI commands `yarn test:other`, `yarn test:code` and `yarn test:typecheck`, which match the truth; `yarn fix` is only an extra auto-fix note.

q5.reason: It names yarn.lock, the Crowdin-managed non-en locales with only en.json hand-edited, percentages.json and the build output dirs, all matching the truth; the extra vendored items are harmless.
